section: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi - Kubja Vishnuvardhana, dynastic history, patronage of Telugu (Nannaya)
subsections: End of the dynasty - Chalukya-Chola merger

accepted.s: Kulothunga I became the Chola king in which year?
accepted.x: Kulothunga I became the Chola king in 1070 CE. He subsequently inherited the Chalukya kingdom in 1075 CE.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical distinction between accession to the Chola throne and inheritance of the Chalukya kingdom.
accepted.sec: End of the dynasty - Chalukya-Chola merger

accepted.s: Kulothunga I was the son of whom?
accepted.x: Kulothunga I was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a ruler's parentage and other prominent names associated with the dynasty.
accepted.sec: End of the dynasty - Chalukya-Chola merger

accepted.s: The campaign of Kulothunga I against Kalinga was recorded in which work?
accepted.x: Kulothunga I's campaign against Kalinga was recorded in Kalingattupparani, composed by Jayangondar.
accepted.tq: Match the military campaign with its literary record rather than with another work associated with the period.
accepted.sec: End of the dynasty - Chalukya-Chola merger

accepted.x: Jayangondar composed Kalingattupparani, which records Kulothunga I's campaign against Kalinga.
accepted.tq: Use the author–work association and distinguish it from poets and scholars connected with Telugu literature.
accepted.sec: End of the dynasty - Chalukya-Chola merger

accepted.s: Kulothunga I sent how many merchants to China?
accepted.x: Kulothunga I sent 72 merchants to China.
accepted.tq: Check the exact numerical figure instead of relying on the surrounding dates of the dynasty.
accepted.sec: End of the dynasty - Chalukya-Chola merger

accepted.s: Which one of the following was built by Kulothunga I at Visakhapatnam?
accepted.x: Kulothunga I built Kulothunga Cholapuram at Visakhapatnam. Rajamahendri and Pedavegi were capitals associated with the Eastern Chalukya territory, while Venginadu denotes the core region.
accepted.tq: Apply the location clue and reject nearby capital and territorial names.
accepted.sec: End of the dynasty - Chalukya-Chola merger

accepted.s: Which of the following best expresses the major cultural significance of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: They confined literary activity exclusively to Sanskrit.
They ended the use of Telugu in the Vengi region.
They turned Telugu into a literary language.
They replaced Telugu with Tamil as the court language.
accepted.x: A major significance of the Eastern Chalukyas was that they helped turn Telugu into a literary language and laid the foundation for Telugu literature.
accepted.tq: Identify the positive cultural consequence and reject absolute or reversed statements.

accepted.s:
With reference to the chronology of the Eastern Chalukya and Chalukya-Chola traditions, arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Beginning of Eastern Chalukya rule
B. Kulothunga I becomes Chola king
C. Kulothunga I inherits the Chalukya kingdom
D. Extended end date under the Chalukya-Chola interpretation
accepted.x: The sequence is 624 CE, 1070 CE, 1075 CE and 1189 CE. Thus, the correct order is A, B, C, D.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two closely related events of 1070 and 1075.

accepted.s: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled Andhra for approximately how long according to the conventional 624–1075 CE chronology?
o: About four and a half centuries
accepted.x: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled Andhra for about four and a half centuries, from 624 to 1075 CE.
accepted.tq: Convert the stated chronological range into its approximate duration.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the core territory and capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: The Pennar-Tungabhadra doab; Kalyana, Warangal and Devagiri
The Godavari-Narmada region; Pataliputra, Ujjain and Kannauj
The Krishna-Godavari doab; Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry
The Krishna-Godavari doab; Kanchi, Madurai and Tanjavur
accepted.x: The core territory was the Krishna-Godavari doab, known as Venginadu. The capitals included Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry.
accepted.tq: Separate the correct territorial region from similarly named South Indian political centres.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects the differing interpretations regarding the end of the Eastern Chalukya line?
1. The conventional date for the end of the proper Eastern Chalukya dynasty is 1075 CE.
2. Some interpretations extend the line to 1189 CE by including the Chalukya-Chola phase.
3. The difference results from whether the Chalukya-Chola phase is included in the dynastic reckoning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1075 CE date excludes the later Chalukya-Chola phase, whereas the 1189 CE interpretation includes that phase in the dynastic reckoning.
accepted.tq: Read the date question as a classification issue and connect each date with the basis of the interpretation.
